definition: The drawing of a sound's amplitude over time.
note: Ardour cs uses 'průběhová křivka' and Audacity cs plain 'křivka'. Neither is used here because 'křivka' is reserved for analysis curves, which are drawn along the waveform. 'Časový/vlnový průběh signálu' is the textbook phrase; in speech 'waveform' or 'vlna' is common.

definition: A picture of how a sound's frequency content changes over time: time across, frequency up, level as colour.
A frequency scale spaced as pitch is heard: roughly linear below 1 kHz and logarithmic above.
note: Unit 'mel'. ČVUT speech-processing lectures also say 'melodická stupnice'.

definition: The moving line that marks the current playback position.
note: Ardour cs ('ukazatel přehrávání', also 'ukazatel polohy'). Keep 'kurzor' for the edit cursor. The app name Playhead stays untranslated.

definition: The position where editing and playback start, set by clicking.
note: Ardour cs translates 'edit point' as 'pracovní bod'.

definition: Samples per second of a digital sound, in Hz.
note: LMMS cs 'vzorkovací frekvence'; Audacity cs and ČSN usage 'vzorkovací kmitočet'.

definition: Bits per sample of a digital sound; sets its resolution.
note: Audacity cs.

definition: One signal of a sound file; stereo has two.
One channel.
Two channels, left and right.
Stereo written as the sum (mid) and the difference (side) of the channels.
note: Engineers say 'M/S' or 'mid/side'; textbooks say 'signál M (součtový) a S (rozdílový)', as in 'MS stereofonie'.

definition: Where in its cycle a wave is at a given moment.
Whether a signal is upright or inverted.
note: Use 'obrátit polaritu' (Ardour cs) and not 'obrátit fázi' when the signal is simply inverted.

definition: How strong a signal is, usually in dB.
note: 'Úroveň signálu' is the audio-engineering term (also in RRTV EBU R 128 cz). 'Hladina' is the ČSN term for logarithmic acoustic quantities (hladina akustického tlaku), so use it only for dB SPL. Never 'hlasitost', which is loudness.

definition: A change of level, in dB.
note: 'Zesílení' is used in LMMS and Audacity cs, 'Zisk' in Ardour cs. A negative gain is still 'zesílení' (e.g. −6 dB); 'zeslabení' only in running text.

definition: The largest absolute sample value.
note: 'Špičková úroveň' in RRTV EBU R 128 cz and in Czech metering (špičkový měřič). Audacity and Ardour cs use 'vrchol'. In this vocabulary 'vrchol' is kept for the top of an envelope or curve.

definition: The peak of the signal between samples, as a DAC would reproduce it.
note: RRTV Czech translations of EBU R 128 and Tech 3341 ('maximální skutečná špičková úroveň'). The unit stays dBTP.

definition: How loud a sound is heard, as opposed to its level.
note: Used in ČSN ISO 532-1, in RRTV EBU R 128 cz ('hlasitost pořadu', 'integrovaná hlasitost') and in Ardour/Audacity cs.

definition: Loudness units relative to full scale (ITU-R BS.1770); 1 LU is 1 dB.
note: RRTV EBU R 128 cz expands it as 'jednotka hlasitosti vztažená k celému rozsahu'.

definition: The frequency weighting that loudness meters apply before measuring.
note: RRTV Czech translation of EBU Tech 3341 ('frekvenční váhování'). For A/C weighting, Czech acoustics texts also write 'kmitočtové vážení' or 'váhový filtr'.
alternatives: váhový filtr K; kmitočtové vážení K

definition: Set a sound's peak or loudness to a target.
note: Audacity and Ardour cs 'Normalizovat'; noun 'normalizace hlasitosti' (RRTV, Audacity).

definition: A gradual change of level at the start (fade-in) or end (fade-out).
note: Czech engineers say fade, fade-in, fade-out (pl. 'fady'). Ardour cs uses 'Postupné zesílení/zeslabení signálu', and Audacity cs 'Fade In (postupný náběh)' / 'Fade Out (do ztracena)'. 'Náběh' is avoided because it means attack here, and 'prolínání' because it means crossfade.
alternatives: postupné zesílení / postupné zeslabení; postupná změna úrovně

definition: Distortion when a signal exceeds the largest value that can be stored.
note: Audacity cs ('Přebuzení', 'Najít přebuzení'). This is the everyday engineering word; technically the digital mechanism is 'ořezání (limitace) signálu'.

definition: A constant shift of the signal away from zero.
note: Audacity cs ('Odstranit stejnosměrnou složku'); standard electrical-engineering term.

definition: The level of the background noise under a sound.
note: Usual engineering phrase, e.g. 'šumové pozadí −90 dB'. Audacity cs 'nežádoucí hluk' is not adopted.

definition: A stretch with no sound above the noise floor.
A sound that ends before its decay has died away.
note: Uses 'doznění' for tail, as in all tail-related entries.

definition: One recorded or rendered version of a sound.
note: Czech studio usage is the loan 'take' (spoken 'tejk'). Ardour cs uses 'záběr' (film sense) or 'verze'. Keep it undeclined in UI where possible ('Take 3').

definition: Compute a processed sound and write it as audio.
note: Common studio usage. Audacity cs 'Spojit' (Mix and Render) is too vague. Noun: 'render'.

definition: A sound that repeats without an audible join.
A fade-out of one sound overlapping a fade-in of another.
note: Used in Audacity, Ardour and LMMS cs. 'Prolnutí' for one instance.

definition: Cut a sound into parts at chosen points.
note: Producers also say 'slicovat'/'nasekat'. One resulting part is a 'díl' or 'výřez'.

definition: Change a sound's duration without changing its pitch.
note: Like English 'stretch', this covers shortening too. Ardour cs has 'Protáhnutí času'; theses often keep 'time-stretching'.

definition: Change a sound's pitch without changing its duration.
note: Ardour cs ('Posun výšky tónu').

definition: The unit of loudness as heard; 1 sone is the loudness of a 1 kHz tone at 40 dB SPL.
note: ISO 532-1. Czech texts name the unit 'son' (pl. 'sony', e.g. 'Jednotka hlasitosti je son', ZČU thesis). The unit is kept as 'sone' per this vocabulary's rule.

definition: How much a sound's energy sits at high frequencies, as heard; in acum.
note: DIN 45692. Standard Czech psychoacoustic term ('hlasitost, ostrost a drsnost', Czech music-acoustics research, RIV 2006). Reserved, so 'ostrý' must not be used for harshness.

definition: The rasping quality of fast amplitude modulation (about 15–300 Hz); in asper.
note: 'Drsnost' is used in Czech psychoacoustic research on musical signals; some theses (ZČU) say 'hrubost'. Reserved, so 'drsný' must not be used for harshness.

definition: The sensation of slow amplitude modulation (about 1–20 Hz, strongest near 4 Hz); in vacil.
note: Both 'síla fluktuace' and 'fluktuační síla' (ZČU thesis) occur.

definition: Zwicker's combination of loudness, sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength into one annoyance value.
note: 'Obtěžování' is the ČSN term for noise annoyance (ČSN ISO 1996-1). 'Nepříjemnost' is left for harshness, which is derived from it.

definition: One sound making another harder or impossible to hear.
The frequency range the ear integrates as one; on the Bark scale.
note: Standard ('kritická pásma slyšení', 'Barkova stupnice').

definition: A value drawn over time along the waveform.
A small picture of a whole sound used to find one's way in it.
The overview of one sound as Playhead draws it: waveform, curves and marks in one band.
note: Chosen so that a 'pás' (strip) contains 'pruhy' (lanes), as in a road with lanes. 'Proužek' is friendlier but diminutive; 'lišta' suggests a toolbar; 'strip' is clear to DAW users but does not decline well.

definition: A named way to draw a strip, written as a short code of layers.
note: 'Vzhled' reads most naturally ('Vzhled: klasický', 'Kód vzhledu'), but Firefox cs calls themes 'Vzhledy'. If chosen, name colour themes 'barevný motiv' to keep look ≠ theme. 'Podoba' avoids the clash but sounds less natural in UI.

definition: The short text that defines a look, for example "form:overlay,shape:mirror,lane:harshness".
note: Follows the choice for 'look'. The code's keys and values are not translated.
alternatives: kód podoby; zápis vzhledu; look code

definition: One element of a look: a waveform, spectrogram, curve, set of marks or sections.
note: The usual word, also used in Ardour cs for overlaid/stacked layers. The same word is used for sound layers in 'remix vrstev'; context separates them. 'Prvek' is vaguer but would avoid that overlap.

definition: A horizontal band of a strip that holds one curve.
note: Ardour cs ('pruh automatizace' = automation lane); also 'jízdní pruh' = traffic lane.

definition: Curves drawn in one shared band instead of separate lanes.
note: Ardour cs 'Překryto' (overlaid layer display). Neuter, agreeing with 'zobrazení'. 'Přes sebe' is the clearest toggle label. Distinct from 'zrcadlené' (mirrored).
alternatives: přes sebe; v jednom pruhu; překrývající se

definition: Drawn symmetrically above and below a centre line, like a waveform.
note: Neuter, agreeing with 'zobrazení'; use 'zrcadlený průběh' etc. when agreeing with a masculine noun.

definition: Drawn upwards from the bottom of the band.
note: Adverbial phrase, used as a mode label next to 'zrcadlené' and 'překryté'.
alternatives: od spodní hrany; od základní čáry

definition: A compact chart that folds a curve into coloured bands of increasing intensity.
note: No established Czech term found; this is a calque. Czech data-visualisation texts usually keep 'horizon chart'.

definition: A waveform whose height follows a curve, for example perceived loudness, instead of the peak level.
note: 'Tvarovaný' (shaped) is neutral and clear. 'Modelovaný' is closer to sculpting but clashes with the physical models in Workbench (model nárazu). The loan would be unusual.
alternatives: modelovaný vlnový průběh; vytvarovaný průběh; sculpted waveform

definition: The ordinary peak waveform drawn as a thin line behind another layer.
Ticks along the strip at events, onsets, beats or section boundaries.
note: Ardour cs uses 'Značka' for marker. Plural noun.

definition: The text that says what each colour and line of a strip shows.
How much Playhead analyses: fast (curves only), sound effect, or music.
A number or curve computed from a sound that describes one of its properties.
note: Czech MIR usage ('zvukové deskriptory').

definition: A descriptor used as input to a classifier or search.
note: Czech pattern-recognition term ('příznakový vektor', 'kepstrální příznaky', ČVUT).

definition: How much is happening: spectral change and the density of events.
note: 'Aktivita' is clear and fits UI phrases. 'Dění' is the most idiomatic ('kolik se toho děje') but awkward as a curve name. 'Ruch' is avoided because 'ruchy' means Foley.

definition: How exciting or calming a sound is, after the psychological dimension of the same name.
note: Czech psychology often keeps the loan ('valence a arousal', declined 'arousalu') or uses 'excitace'. 'Aktivace' is avoided next to 'aktivita' (activity).

definition: How unpleasant a sound is to listen to, computed from psychoacoustic annoyance; not the same as roughness.
note: The everyday Czech words for 'harsh' (ostrý, drsný) are taken by sharpness and roughness. 'Nepříjemnost' follows the definition and differs from 'obtěžování' (annoyance), its input. 'Tvrdost' is idiomatic in mixing but clashes with material hardness in Workbench. 'Drásavost' is expressive but close to roughness.

definition: Build-up and release over time, after the model of musical tension by Farbood (2012).
note: The surname is left uninflected with a feminine verb (modern usage), instead of 'Farboodová'.

definition: How far the harmony is from rest, from the tonal interval space.
note: 'Tonální intervalový prostor' is a calque of tonal interval space (Bernardes et al. 2016).

definition: How much a moment differs from what came before.
note: Foote 2000; 'křivka novosti' for the novelty curve. Kept apart from 'spektrální překvapení' and 'překvapivost'.

definition: Change of the spectrum that loudness does not explain.
note: Parallels the English and stays distinct from 'novost' (novelty) and 'překvapivost' (surprisal) by word form. 'Nečekaná změna spektra' is clearer but long. 'Spektrální zvrat' is short but suggests a reversal.
alternatives: nečekaná změna spektra; spektrální zvrat; spectral surprise

definition: Information content of an event: the less expected, the higher.
note: In Czech information theory the quantity is 'vlastní informace' (self-information); 'překvapivost' is the readable UI name. Note the pair překvapivost (surprisal) / spektrální překvapení (spectral surprise).

definition: Where a piece moves to a new part, signed: up where sound enters, down where it falls away or breaks off.
note: 'Strukturní změna' is a literal, neutral term that suits a signed curve. 'Předěl' is idiomatic for a move to a new part but suggests a point, not a curve. 'Strukturální' is also correct. 'Vstupuje' is used for 'enters' so as not to clash with 'nástup' (onset).

definition: How clearly a regular pulse is felt at each moment.
note: Calque of Grosche and Müller's (predominant) local pulse. Avoid 'síla doby' (beat strength).

definition: The moment a sound or note begins.
note: Czech MIR says 'nástup (tónu)' or 'detekce nástupů', often alongside 'onset'. A moment, kept apart from 'náběh' (attack, a phase) and 'tranzient'.

definition: How strongly new sound arrives at each moment; peaks are hits.
One distinct sound within a file, such as a hit, a step or a creak, with a start and an end.
The first part of a sound, from its start to its peak.
note: Czech music acoustics divides a tone into náběh, ustálená část and doznívání; LMMS and Audacity cs also use 'náběh'. Engineers often say 'attack'. A phase, kept apart from 'nástup' (onset, a moment).

definition: The sustained, often tonal, part of a sound after its attack.
note: Engineers say 'tělo' (e.g. the body of a snare); music acoustics says 'ustálená část'.

definition: The part of a sound in which it dies away.
note: Czech music-acoustics term. Synth ADSR 'decay' is 'pokles' (LMMS cs), which is a different meaning.

definition: The late part of a decay, including reverberation.
note: 'Ocas' (as in 'ocas dozvuku') is common studio slang but sounds odd in UI. 'Doznění' is neutral and works in the tool names (rozšířit doznění, dozvuk na doznění).

definition: A short, fast change of level and spectrum, typically at an attack.
note: Engineers say 'tranzient/transient' (pl. 'tranzienty'); physics and electronics say 'přechodový jev'. Ardour cs 'přechod' is not adopted (too vague).

definition: The regular pulse a listener taps along to.
note: Ardour cs ('Takty a doby') and Czech MIR theses. 'Úder' is reserved for hits.

definition: The first beat of a bar.
note: 'Těžká doba' is broader (any strong beat).

definition: A group of beats, usually four.
note: Ardour cs. Not to be confused with the shape 'tyč' (bar-shape).

definition: The speed of the beat, in beats per minute (BPM).
note: Czech expansion of BPM: 'úderů za minutu' (Audacity cs).

definition: A part of a piece, such as an intro or chorus, found from where its sound changes.
note: 'Část' is too generic for a UI term; producers also say 'sekce'.

definition: How much a sound returns to states it has been in before.
note: As in 'rekurentní diagram' (recurrence plot, Marwan et al. 2007).

definition: How often a pattern repeats, in Hz.
How strongly a sound is periodic (pitched) rather than noisy.
How steadily a sound's phases advance; 1 for a steady tone, near 0 for noise.
How much a sound changes when played backwards; high for hits that decay.
note: 'Šipka času' is the established Czech phrase for the physical arrow of time, so it carries the same image. 'Časová nevratnost' is the technical term (docs only, as in the source). 'Směr času' is plainer but loses the idea of a degree.
alternatives: časová nevratnost; směr času; time arrow

definition: How much a sound consists of clicks, cracks and crackle, from spectral kurtosis.
note: ČSN ISO 1996-1 uses 'impulzivnost' for impulsive noise, so the word is established in acoustics. 'Praskavost' is vivid but covers only crackle. Avoid 'špičatost' (= kurtosis).

definition: A statistic that is 0 for steady noise, −1 for a steady tone and large for clicks.
note: Czech machine-diagnostics usage of Antoni's spectral kurtosis; 'špičatost' is the general statistics word for kurtosis.

definition: How fast the spectrum's centre moves up or down, in octaves per second.
note: 'Pohyb spektra' is natural Czech. 'Spektrální pohyb' mirrors the English and the other 'spektrální' terms. 'Posun těžiště spektra' is exact but long.
alternatives: spektrální pohyb; posun těžiště spektra; spectral motion

definition: The centre of mass of a spectrum; a measure of brightness.
note: 'Spektrální centroid' is the usual term in Czech MIR theses; 'těžiště spektra' in psychoacoustics.

definition: Spectral change that does not move the centre, as when a spectrum spreads or narrows.
note: 'Přetváření' is short and pairs with 'pohyb spektra'. 'Změna tvaru spektra' is self-explanatory but long.
alternatives: změna tvaru spektra; přeskupení spektra; reshaping

definition: Whether events come regularly (below 0), at random (0) or in bursts (above 0).
note: No established Czech term. Based on 'shluk' = burst (as in telecom 'shlukové chyby'); 'nárazovitost' (cf. 'nárazový provoz') is the other option.

definition: How evenly a sound's energy is spread over time.
The time a sound takes to fall by 60 dB.
note: For rooms the ČSN EN ISO 3382 term is 'doba dozvuku'. Here it is the sound's own decay, hence 'doznívání'.

definition: How quickly a vibrating body loses energy.
What an impacted object is made of, as heard: damped, glass-like or metal-like.
One frequency component of a sound.
note: Czech music-acoustics term.

definition: A partial above the lowest one.
note: 'Alikvotní tón' is the more common word but implies harmonic partials. The definition includes inharmonic ones (bells), so the neutral 'svrchní tón' is preferred (cf. 'zpěv svrchních tónů').

definition: With partials that are not whole-number multiples of a fundamental, as in bells and struck metal.
Automatic checks for clipping, DC offset, silence and cut tails.
A test that edits a sound in a known way and checks that the analysis changes as it must.
note: 'Samokontrola' describes what it does. 'Autotest' is familiar but suggests a hardware power-on test. Avoid 'jednotkový test' (unit test).

definition: A tool that turns down resonances only while the sound is harsh.
note: Infinitive command. 'Zjemnit' (make gentler) is short and idiomatic but does not echo 'nepříjemnost'. 'Zmírnit nepříjemnost' is transparent but long. A de-esser stays 'de-esser' in Czech.

definition: A tool that splits a sound into its transient part and its sustained part, to rebalance them.
note: Noun-phrase tool title, reusing the terms for attack and body. 'Tranzienty a tělo' is closer to how engineers talk but mixes registers. Not 'tvarovač tranzientů' (transient shaper).
alternatives: tranzienty a tělo; rozdělení náběhu a těla; attack & body

definition: A tool that separates a sound into layers and mixes them again at new levels.
note: 'Remix' is fully naturalised in Czech. 'Přemixování' stresses the action; 'nové smíchání' is plain but wordy.

definition: A tool that turns the tension curve into gain and brightness automation.
note: 'Tvarovač' is the usual calque of 'shaper' (tvarovač obálky/tranzientů). 'Tvarování' is the process noun. 'Napětí do automatizace' says what it does.
alternatives: tvarování napětí; napětí do automatizace; tension shaper

definition: A tool that finds and crossfades loop points where the sound repeats best.
note: 'Tvorba smyček' reads as a tool title. 'Tvůrce smyček' is the literal agent noun. 'Smyčkovač' is playful and short but nonstandard.

definition: Several slightly different versions of one sound, to avoid repetition in games.
note: 'Variace' also has a musical-form meaning. Plural noun.

definition: A tool that repairs what the quality checks flag before a sound is exported.
note: Noun-phrase tool title; Ardour cs uses 'Vyčistit' for clean-up. Playhead names the tool with a verb ('Clean up for export'), so the app uses the infinitive 'Vyčistit pro export', as for the other command-style tools.
alternatives: úprava před exportem; vyčistit pro export

definition: Reverberation fed only from the decays of the events, keeping the attacks dry.
note: 'Dozvuk' = reverb (Audacity cs). 'Dozvuk na doznění' is compact; 'jen z doznění' states the feed more exactly; 'na ocasy' is studio slang.
alternatives: dozvuk jen z doznění; dozvuk na ocasy; reverb on the tails

definition: Saturation applied only to the events' attacks or bodies.
note: Infinitive command. 'Saturovat' says exactly what happens. 'Nabudit' keeps the 'drive' image (buzení) and is idiomatic, but sounds close to 'přebuzení' (clipping).
alternatives: nabudit údery; saturace úderů; drive the hits

definition: A tool that lengthens or shortens how long each event rings after its peak.
note: Most natural Czech, but close to 'doba doznívání (T60)'. Choose 'délka znění' if a lexical distinction from the measured value is wanted; 'znění' also means 'wording'.

definition: A tool that evens out how loud the events are, one gain per event, without touching their shape.
note: Infinitive command, matching 'vyrovnanost' (evenness). Not 'komprimovat'. 'Srovnat hlasitost' is more explicit but longer.
alternatives: vyrovnání událostí; srovnat hlasitost událostí; level the events

definition: Turn stereo into mono with the channels' phase lined up, so nothing cancels.
note: Infinitive command. 'Sloučit' is the natural verb; 'složit' is the literal calque of 'fold' but also means 'compose'. Keep 'sečíst do mona' for the plain sum (Audacity cs: 'Smíchání do mono').
alternatives: složit do mona; sloučení do mona; fold to mono

definition: Make or widen stereo only after the attacks, keeping attacks centred and the result mono-compatible.
note: Infinitive command using 'doznění' for tails; 'ocasy' is slang.
alternatives: rozšíření doznění; rozšířit ocasy; widen the tails

definition: Turn more channels into fewer.
note: The loan is standard in Czech broadcast and post-production (e.g. downmix 5.1 do sterea).

definition: How well a stereo sound survives being summed to mono.
Making two signals less alike while keeping their spectrum, to widen a stereo image.
Regular notches in a spectrum when a signal is summed with a delayed copy of itself.
note: 'Hřebenový filtr' in ČVUT audio-processing lectures.

definition: Loss of level when signals of opposite phase are summed.
note: Engineering usage: 'signály se v protifázi vyruší'.

definition: A faint smear of a sound before its attack, caused by frame-based processing.
note: Calque; no authoritative Czech source found, and codec literature often keeps 'pre-echo'.

definition: An equaliser: a filter that changes the level of frequency bands.
note: 'EQ' is used as is in UI and speech; 'korekce' is the older hi-fi term.

definition: An EQ whose band gains follow the level in each band.
Parameter changes over time, recorded or drawn.
note: Ardour cs.

definition: A processor that turns loud passages down by a ratio above a threshold.
The level above which a processor acts.
note: Audacity, Ardour and LMMS cs.

definition: How strongly a compressor turns the level down above its threshold.
note: Audacity and LMMS cs.

definition: How fast a processor reacts when the level rises.
note: Audacity cs uses 'Čas náběhu' and LMMS cs 'Náběh'. Czech engineers mostly say 'attack' (e.g. muzikus.cz), so it is offered in alt for a loan-style UI.

definition: How fast a processor recovers when the level falls.
note: Audacity cs uses 'Čas uvolnění'. LMMS cs 'Doznění' belongs to envelopes and is not used here. Engineers mostly say 'release'.

definition: A processor or condition that opens only above a threshold.
note: Audacity and Ardour cs use 'Brána'. For the gate in loudness measurement, RRTV EBU R 128 cz uses 'hradlování' and 'hradlované měření'.

definition: Soft distortion that adds harmonics and rounds peaks.
Audible rise and fall of the background caused by a compressor.
How alike the events are in loudness.
Effects applied one after another to a sound.
A saved set of settings.
note: Ardour and LMMS cs use 'předvolba'; Audacity cs uses 'přednastavení'.

definition: A gradual blend from one sound into another.
note: Avoid 'prolnutí', which means crossfade.

definition: Combining the spectrum of one sound with the envelope or excitation of another.
Filtering one sound by another, for example by a room's impulse response.
Giving one sound the level envelope of another.
Multiplying two signals, which creates sum and difference frequencies.
Built from many short grains of sound.
A short added sound placed at a moment of another sound to emphasise it.
note: 'Akcent' is a familiar musical term and countable ('přidat akcent'). 'Zvýraznění' describes the effect, not the added sound. 'Důraz' is uncountable.

definition: A part of the app that makes new sounds from parameters.
A sound generator built from oscillators, noise, envelopes and filters.
note: Colloquially 'synťák'; not for UI.

definition: A physical model of a struck object of a given material and shape.
note: 'Úder' is reserved for hits (events).

definition: Rebuilding a sound from parameters measured on it, such as its partials and decays.
Made of resonant modes, each with a frequency and a decay.
note: As in 'modální syntéza'; acoustics also says 'vlastní módy/vidy'.

definition: A continuous sound made of many small events, such as rain, fire or gravel.
A generator in which an action, such as an object moving or a force, drives the sound of a medium that responds to it (gravel, water, air).
note: Echoes Newton's 'zákon akce a reakce', which every Czech knows from school. 'Působení a odezva' sounds more technical. 'Odezva' fits 'response' but is also the word for impulse response. 'Budí' (excites) renders 'drives', as in physical models.
alternatives: působení a odezva; akce a odezva; action & reaction

definition: What reacts to an action: gravel, leaves, water, air, sparks or a force field.
note: 'Prostředí' is the physics word for medium but also means environment or ambience.

definition: A curve that controls a sound's parameters over time.
note: 'Drive' here means control, not overdrive, so 'řídicí' (controlling) is clearest. 'Budicí' (exciting) fits physical models but suggests saturation drive.
alternatives: budicí křivka; křivka řízení; drive curve

definition: How slowly a reaction settles after the action stops.
Everyday sounds performed and recorded in sync with picture.
note: Czech film-sound term; the Foley artist is a 'ruchař'. The English 'foley' is also used (filmvychova.cz, Rosebud). Plural noun.

definition: The background sound of a place.
note: Czech film-sound term ('atmosféry'; slang 'atmoska').

definition: A short sound played once, such as a hit or a UI click.
note: Loan used by Czech sound designers and sample libraries.

definition: The sound of something moving fast past the listener.
note: Sound designers use the loan. 'Svist' is the Czech word for the sound and fits a more localised UI.

definition: The last steps before export: format, channels, fades and level.

note: 'Lepenka' is the technical term; 'karton' is everyday.
'Pryž' is the technical term; 'guma' is everyday.

definition: A long solid body, such as a rod or beam.
note: Not to be confused with the musical bar ('takt').

definition: A thin flat body.
A stretched skin, as on a drum.
A thin curved body, such as a can or pot.
A stiff string or wire that rings with slightly stretched (inharmonic) partials.
note: 'Drát' follows the English choice of 'wire'. In Workbench the impact-model shape 'Wire / string' becomes 'Drát / struna'. 'Roztažené' is the usual Czech for stretched partials (as in piano-string inharmonicity).

definition: A hollow body with flat sides.
note: 'Skříň' as in 'rezonanční skříň'; 'krabice' is everyday and suggests cardboard.
